title: gymnocarpium robertianum subsp. longulum

It is a rare, perennial plant native to certain regions of Europe and Asia, characterized by its delicate fronds and unique growth habit. The long-stalked oak fern has been traditionally used in herbal medicine due to its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to reduce stress and improve overall well-being. The plant contains bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which may contribute to its therapeutic actions, including antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects.
